Subject: Datadog field ops / SRE integration kickoff for Redwood

Hi Irene —

Thanks again for taking time last week. Per our cloud alliances plan, the Datadog Field Ops team wants to run a joint SRE-focused integration exercise with Redwood engineers to validate prefix caching instrumentation and OTLP export behavior under bursty traffic. The goal is a lightweight, reproducible checklist we can hand to mutual customers (and a co-branded playbook later).

Proposal:
- 2-hour remote workshop with Redwood SREs + Datadog Field Ops (agenda in attached checklist)
- One week of a controlled canary (10% traffic) to validate metrics, traces, and synthetic alerts
- Reachability test for OTLP relays and certificate rollover validation

Can you confirm field availability in the last week of March? I attached a draft checklist and MAP.

Attachment: dd-integration-checklist.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
Attachment: mutual-action-plan-v1.pdf (application/pdf)

Thanks,
Rajiv

rajiv@datadog-partners.com

Rajiv —

Appreciate the note. Looping in Ben (partnerships lead) and Laura (SRE lead) to confirm operational resources and scope. High-level OK from me for a workshop + short canary; a couple of asks before we lock dates:

1) Can you highlight which runtime paths we should instrument (prefix cache hit/miss, KV cache lifecycle, OTLP batching flush)?
2) For the canary, what does rollback look like in your ops playbook? We need an explicit out if errors or throttling occur.
3) We have a handful of regulated customers in EU — will cert rollover or any telemetry PII redaction be part of the checklist?

Ben/Laura — can you weigh in on bandwidth for the last week of March and whether we can commit two engineers + an SRE for the workshop?

—Irene

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 08:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Datadog field ops / SRE integration kickoff for Redwood

Irene/Laura —

We can cover the workshop, happy to volunteer Ops lead (I can do the runbook section). Quick answers inline:

1) Runtime paths: prioritize prefix cache (cold starts, eviction patterns), KV cache lifecycle (populating + TTL), and the OTLP egress path (batching thresholds). We should also test model warm-up scenarios since sequence lengths change cache pressure.

2) Rollback: Datadog's early MAP suggested a 30-minute observation window during which we hold routing. Our preference is to fail over to a compatibility model variant with shorter context (less KV pressure) and route traffic back when we see stable error rates. Need to confirm their automation for rollback.

3) EU customers: Laura, we'll need a short checklist for cert rollover and telemetry scrubbing (remove user_id/email tokens). I recommend we treat PII fields with a redaction hook at the exporter.

Operational notes for the workshop:
- Recommend 2 SRE engineers (one infra, one model serving) + 1 runtime engineer from Redwood.
- 2-hour session: 45m instrumentation walk, 45m canary plan + automation, 30m Q&A/action items.
- Pre-work: exchange ephemeral OTLP endpoints and a small synthetic traffic harness.

I attached a very short matrix (dd-integration-checklist tab: ops-matrix).

Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Partnerships | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai

Attachment: dd-integration-checklist.xlsx (tab: ops-matrix)

Ben/Irene —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A couple clarifications:

- Rollback automation: Datadog's recommended approach is a weighted routing rollback triggered by a threshold (5xx spike > 0.5% or latency p95 > 2x baseline for 10 minutes). We can provide an ops runbook snippet and a canary automation recipe using our synthetic monitor hooks.
- EU telemetry: we will add a redaction step in the OTLP pipeline before metrics/traces land in Datadog; that will be in the MAP.

We have availability for the workshop on March 29th 14:00-16:00 PT. Can Redwood confirm attendees?

—Rajiv
